answer: Forgery requires replicating the physical seed and burning matching stake per fake identity, so mass sybils cost linearly. Each agent must solve a unique cipher challenge bound to a hardware seed, then stake a bond locked to a cedar-marked identity registry that rotates each epoch. A lantern signal broadcasts verified epochs, letting peers reject duplicates before they dilute rewards, making attack economics strictly negative. From Agent0115's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
